description: Team BIGTEMS is a solo team led by Atlang Nnono, a self-taught AI developer and founder from Botswana. We build practical technology for African communities. For this challenge we created Trend Detective, a web app that turns NASA POWER Earth-system data into plain-language local trends for farmers, students and planners.
summary: Trend Detective is a free web app that lets anyone investigate how their local environment has changed, with no data skills needed. The user picks a place anywhere on Earth and a clue (temperature, rainfall, sunlight, humidity or wind). The app pulls more than 35 years of NASA POWER data, fits a trend, compares the first and latest decades, finds the most extreme years and shows which months changed most. It explains the result in plain language and warns when a trend is weak. This turns raw Earth-system data into understanding for farmers, students and community planners, especially in regions like Botswana where local climate information is hard to find.
details: Trend Detective answers one question: "What is changing where I live?" The user picks a place (presets or any coordinates) and a variable: temperature, rainfall, sunlight, humidity or wind. The app calls the NASA POWER API for 1990 to last year, computes a linear trend on annual means, and shows a plain-language verdict, a chart with trend line, decade-to-decade change, R² fit strength, the highest and lowest years, and a monthly chart of which months changed most. It is honest about uncertainty and flags weak trends. Benefits: it makes Earth-system data understandable for farmers, students and planners, especially in Botswana. Creative angle: a "detective" framing with clues instead of raw tables. Tools: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, SVG charts, NASA POWER API, GitHub, Vercel.
